To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the influence of orthodonic treatment on smile esthetics seems to be minimal, and the midline position and smile arc are more important than the axial midline angulations.

four premolar extraction or extraction-free treatment protocols seem to be acceptable in terms of facial esthetics, that dental midline deviation is acceptable up to 2.2mm, that a smile arc of 20 degrees seems to be ideal, and that buccal corridor width is not a factor in smile attractiveness.

orthodontic treatment has a positive effect on smile esthetics when well indicated, that a small midline deviation is acceptable, that a 10deg axial midline angulate is already very apparent and that the buccal corridor size and smile arc alone have little effect on smile esthetic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the scientific evidence of some variables on the smile esthetics.
a limited number of variables, and more research is needed to better understand the influence of other variables on smile attractiveness.
the influence of some orthodontic variables on the esthetics of the smile, and it is our hope that this information will be of use to orthodontists in their daily work.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although there seems to be an effect of some variables on the smile attractiveness, the influence is not as great as one could think.

the variables studied in this systematic review do not seem to have a significant influence on smile esthetics, and that a smile is not only the result of a single variable, but the result of the interaction of all variables.
the smile esthetics of patients treated with premolar extractions are not different from those of patients treated with nonextraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the influence of ortho-dontic treatment, mid-line position, axial mid-line angulation, bucco-corridor, and smile arc is still controversial and needs further research.
orthodontic treatment does not seem to have any effect on smile attractiveness, whereas midline position, smile arc, and buccal corridor size seem to have some effect on smile attractiveness.
the influence of orthognathic surgery on smile esthetics has not been evaluated, and the influence of buccal corridor on smile esthetics should not be neglected in clinical practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single factor that is determinant in the evaluation of smile esthetics.
the influence of these factors on smile attractiveness is not as strong as previously believed.
the variables studied in this review have an influence on smile attractiveness but that their effects are not predictable.
